extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists and physicians (readers of Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical experimental and observational standards for studying natural substances (asbestos, mineral waters, salts) and for pathological dissection; includes how to prepare, test, observe, and report findings. Emphasis on what to observe in situ, during/after sampling, and how to interpret results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for incombustibility of cloth (asbestos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical fire tests: put the cloth into a strong charcoal fire and observe whether, after being red-hot for some considerable time and then cooled, it is little altered; also steep pieces in oil and put them in the fire to see whether they are consumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: a piece heated red-hot in a charcoal fire came forth little altered when cold (only seeming a little whiter and cleaner); an instance where a long rope steeped in oil and put in the fire was not consumed. Use severe trials (oil-soaking, prolonged red-heat) to verify claims of incombustibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacture/process requirements for making amianthus (asbestos) into thread and cloth
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence of processing: the lanuginous mineral is first dried in the sun, pounded in a brass mortar, the earthy part separated from the woolly, the woolly washed to remove impurities, then spun into thread and woven into cloth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional steps reported by other authors: after pounding and shaking off earthy parts, the woolly was combed (argument for some longer fibres). Cleansing of foul or spotted cloth can be done by 'throwing it into the fire' for an hour's time. Preparation techniques (e.g., Marco Antonio Castagna) can render the material tractable and soft, resembling lamb's skin or paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification criteria for amianthus/asbestos (physical characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical features: woolly part white silver in colour; threads very fine and slender yet ponderous; smallest particles, when thoroughly wet, sink in water; colours vary (white, cinereous, straw-colour, light blue, sea-green, red, iron-colour); found in various localities (India, Tartary, Cyprus, Wales, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a combination of macroscopic colour and microscopic thread characteristics (fine slender threads that are heavy when wet) and locality/mineral context (veins through rock) to distinguish mineral origin from vegetable fibres. Note reported variability across localities but similarity in woolly portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic explanation of incombustibility (mechanistic criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Asserts that the threads are 'altogether homogeneous, and nothing else but the pure striae of liquid alum, holding nothing of sulphur, bitumen, or water' so that fire can pass through but cannot carry anything from it; homogeneous salts/earths resist fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chemical/physical reasoning: bodies that lack heterogeneous bituminous/sulphurous/aquous particles will not be dilated and thus resist combustion. This is the theoretical criterion offered to account for observed fire-resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three necessary observations for a methodical history of mineral waters
rubrics_metrics.description: 1st. 'That a man ought to take notice of those particulars that relate to it, whilst it is yet under ground, or in its native receptacles.' 2dly. 'To examine the properties and other qualities of it, when it is drawn up by men at the spring head, or other receptacle.' 3dly. 'He is to consider the operation and effects of it on human bodies, whether sick or sound, &c.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boyle uses these three as the organizing standard for descriptive/experimental work on mineral waters and as headings/titles for parts of a treatise. Follow the sequence: record in-situ particulars, then laboratory/spring-head properties, then physiological/therapeutic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of the infusion-of-galls test for mineral waters
rubrics_metrics.description: The infusion of galls only discovers a liquor to be, or not to be, either of a vitriolate or ferruginous nature; it fails to detect many metalline ores and mineral bodies (e.g., decoction of arsenic changes no more upon galls than common water).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on galls-infusion as a universal assay: it's useful principally when iron is the dominant mineral. Examples: strong solution of Roman vitriol where copper predominates produced neither a black nor purplish colour but a thick muddy one. Consider alternative/ additional assays for non-iron minerals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe biological activity with simple infusions (pepper infusion) to detect life/motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Using pepper infusion reveals life and motion of creatures in water; Boyle brings ocular demonstration for the life and motion of those creatures found in water wherein pepper has been infused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an observational diagnostic, infuse samples (e.g., with pepper) and examine microscopically for motile organisms; include such observations when assessing waters' biological character or freshness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use total evaporation residue (caput mortuum) as quantitative indicator of mineral content and purgative strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaporate measured quantities of water and weigh the dry residue; purging mineral waters that are heavier than common water leave a considerable quantity of residuum (example figures: 1 lb of Barnet water yielded 1 dram of white powder; 1 lb Tunbridge water yielded 1 dr. 25 gr.; 1 lb German spa water gave but gr. 1-1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use residue mass as a comparative metric for mineral load and potential pharmacological effect; combine with calculations of impregnation (e.g., one grain of vitriolate substance might impregnate 6000 times its weight of water to produce a purple with galls). Report measured amounts and interpret relative significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe changes during removal/transport (freshness/quickness loss)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boyle notes that the freshness and quickness of certain ferruginous waters that are lighter than common water are much lost in the removal (transport).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sampling mineral waters, record properties at the source and again after transport; account for changes due to exposure/airation in interpreting therapeutic properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about simple classification (avoid rigid acidulae/thermae taxonomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boyle 'dislikes the division of mineral waters into acidulae et thermae' because trials show no manifest acidity in some waters not sulphureous or hot; purgative waters need not contain any single known salt but can be of compounded nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer empirically driven descriptions over simple taxonomies; test for acidity and other properties rather than assuming class membership; consider complex or compounded chemistries when explaining medicinal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autopsy protocol and observations for determining sudden death cause (pathological dissection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic post-mortem examination: inspect liver size and scirrhosities, gall-bladder contents (calculi), spleen size, stomach/pancreas/glands/omentum, kidney firmness, uterus, lungs for adhesions and discoloration, heart condition and fat; upon opening the head examine membranes and blood-vessels (turgid vessels), dissect membranes from affected side, incise the brain substance to find clots, note presence/absence of extravasation in ventricles, weigh cleared cerebrum and cerebellum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correlate anatomical findings with clinical symptoms (e.g., side of head complained of). Use dissection of membranes and incision into brain substance to reveal intracranial clots; document weights and any localized versus generalized lesions; note limitations if precise localization not recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic observational protocol for salts/crystals (Leewenhoek)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation and viewing rules: observations must be made before the water is evaporated; close samples in glass to prevent evaporation; dissolve salts in rain water and view spread thin on a plate; view with microscope and watch growth of figures over time (minutes to hours); note that particles increase in size and may change in colour/translucency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical cautions: if the water is almost gone, many particles run together causing confusion; use rain water for clearer figures; spread very thin to resolve tiny particles; record shapes, relative sizes (compare to hair diameter), and dynamics of growth; take sequential observations (e.g., after minutes, hours, a day's time) and, if needed, manipulate concentration or add reagents (heat, additional salts) to observe transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative/morphological documentation of microscopic particles
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate and report sizes relative to known standards (e.g., fraction of a hair diameter), count numbers in known volumes (e.g., 'more in a quantity of water equal to the weight of a grain than there are stars ... by the naked eye'), and catalogue morphological types observed (e.g., long tapering figures, quadrilateral pyramids, hexagonal pyramids, square sticks, flat figures, four-sided, six-sided, triangular, rhomboidal, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide illustrative figures and comparisons; note how different substances (alum, salt-petre, vitriol, camphor, pot ashes, tin/lead oven ashes) produce characteristic crystalline forms. Use magnification and quantitative analogies to communicate scale and abundance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid post-evaporation observation as primary evidence (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation after substantial evaporation leads to a multitude of particles running together and producing confusion, obscuring the distinct original figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize early observations in dilute solution; prevent evaporation when wanting to observe native particle shapes; if evaporation occurs, interpret aggregated forms cautiously and rely on prior dilute-stage observations for morphology.
